name: Trustworthiness

subjectOf.text: Accuracy alone is insufficient for legal AI: a model must also be explainable before its outputs can be trusted in judicial settings.
subjectOf.abstract: Accuracy alone is insufficient without explainability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: predictive AI used in legal and judicial applications

subjectOf.text: Post hoc explainability techniques do not by themselves establish trustworthiness; the explanations they produce must additionally be verified against human knowledge.
subjectOf.abstract: However, post-hoc explainers still need to be verified for trustworthiness, in that the explanations comport with human knowledge.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: post hoc explainable AI methods such as the SHAP family of explainers

subjectOf.text: When reputation is both the system's aggregation weight and the agent's optimization target, equilibrium behavior includes consistency, collaborative integrity, and systemic stewardship, so the agent learns not merely to perform well but to be trustworthy.
subjectOf.abstract: when reputation is both the system's aggregation weight and the agent's optimization target, the equilibrium behavior includes properties, such as consistency, collaborative integrity, systemic stewardship, that transcend narrow task optimization.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: requires reputation to track trustworthiness properties, not accuracy alone
